data.narrative:
Seneca, a Series A drone and autonomous systems company founded by Stuart Landesberg and Nick Foley, has raised $60M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a sector universe of 8 private peers including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Elroy Air, with no public comparables identified.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable approach, using total raised ($60M) as a valuation proxy and applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage progression. This yields an implied valuation of $120M. Peer-median analysis was not executable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Drones & Autonomous segment—while 5 same-sector peers exist, none yielded three or more datapoints across the applied filters (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier), making sector-wide median comparison unreliable.

The triangulated range derived from available methods is $102M (low), $120M (median), to $138M (high). This single-method result carries material uncertainty: the absence of narrow peer valuation data leaves the analysis reliant on stage progression alone, which may not fully capture Seneca's relative competitive position, unit economics, or technology differentiation within the autonomous systems landscape. Revenue traction and path-to-profitability visibility would significantly sharpen valuation confidence.
